messages:
maria: Heads-up: sample-next-edge CI started failing for a subset of users after the dual-package publish. Error: "require is not defined" in the worker emulation.

tyler: yep saw that in Support. Cond-exports choose cjs branch for some bundlers and CF runtime doesn't have require.

han: also getting reports that TS auto-imports point to wrong .d.ts (editors resolve cjs types) so intellisense is inconsistent.

maria: quick mitigation: update the sample to import 'redwood/edge' explicitly and add a note in the README. I'll PR that now.

tyler: long-term we should: 1) add top-level "types" in package.json, 2) add exports.types mappings per subpath, 3) publish a tiny universal adapter module both ESM/CJS so runtime behavior (auth/retry) is identical.

han: agree. my +1 for adapter module. make it explicit: users import 'redwood/adapter' when they want global fetch shims; we can still import it as a side-effect in the main entrypoint for hosted use cases. Documented behavior is better than magic.

maria: also proposal: add a small 'compat-check' script in samples that tries: require('redwood'), import('redwood'), import('redwood/edge') and prints which entrypoint resolved. Good devex tool.

tyler: can we add a CI job that runs npm pack + node/esbuild/webpack resolution smoke-tests to catch regressions?

han: yes. I'll open tickets for package validation + types mapping RFC.

docs-bot: ticket created: INF-2021 "package exports/types mapping + universal adapter RFC"

maria: ok i'm pushing the sample PR with explicit 'redwood/edge' import and note. Follow-ups in the SDK next sprint.
